chunks: And Ḥanān ibn Sadīr narrated from Muslim ibn Bashīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who married a woman and did not bring witnesses.
He said: “As for what is between him and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then there is nothing against him. But if a tyrannical ruler were to seize him, he would punish him.”

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, before Whom the act is judged
key_terms.امْرَأَةً: a woman, the marriage partner in question
key_terms.سُلْطَانٌ جَائِرٌ: an unjust ruler who enforces punishment wrongfully or coercively

ai.seo_question: Is a marriage without witnesses valid in Islam according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a marriage conducted without witnesses is not sinful in itself before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. However, such a person may still face punishment if apprehended by an unjust ruler. The report concerns a legal ruling related to marriage and the difference between divine validity and coercive political enforcement.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4394 - Hanan ibn Sadir narrated from Muslim ibn Bashir, who reported from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as).
He said: I asked him about a man who married a woman without witnesses.
Imam (as) replied: "As far as what is between him and Allah (swt), the Exalted, there is nothing against him. However, if a tyrannical ruler were to apprehend him, he would punish him."
